messages:
sara: Quick sync — we got a handful of enterprise asks asking for deterministic tail SLOs + automatic model fallback (customer wants guaranteed 95th pctl < 300ms or a fallback to cheaper model). Competitor X just announced something similar. Do we treat this as feature‑parity or an opportunity to differentiate with a config-first routing policy?

alex: framing question — is the ask: strict SLO enforcement at request time or better observability + post-hoc retries? customers sound like they want a runtime guarantee.

mohit: yes runtime. Sales says 3 large customers will only sign if we can offer a "graceful degrade + SLA" story. They want per-route policy: prefer high-quality model, fallback to quantized variant then to smaller model.

julia: infra note: automatic synchronous fallback adds complexity for batching and KV cache invalidation. Could increase p99 latency if not careful. We could do async fallback (return best effort + retry) but that won't satisfy the "single-call guarantee" ask.

danny: sales pressure = high. Customers comparing line-item to Competitor X's announcement. We should at least match parity for sales enablement, but we can push a richer UX: per-tenant policy templates + simulated cost impact.

sara: proposal draft: (1) MVP parity mode: single-call fallback chain, best-effort, documented limited guarantees (SLO only when pinned capacity), (2) Differentiator phase: config-first policies with canary routing, simulated cost/latency preview, and soft-SLA credits. Thoughts on acceptance criteria?

alex: acceptance criteria for MVP: - API change: new field `fallback_chain: [modelA, modelA-quant, modelB]` - behavior: attempt modelA; on modelA capacity error or tail > Xms, synchronously route to next in chain. - E2E latency p95 < 300ms on benchmark suite for medium requests. - No KV cache corruption.

julia: add infra guardrails: - max fallback hops = 3 - per-request budget timeout (e.g., 500ms) - telemetry tags to track which hop served the request.

mohit: shipping risk: modelA-quant might hallucinate more. We need prompt-level evals on parity. Add quality gate: degrade rate < 2% on our eval set or we mark fallback as "low-quality" with an explicit header.

danny: sales ask: include rollback playbook and legal wording for SLA. Without that, customers won't accept.

sara: timeline tradeoff: MVP parity (~4 weeks infra + 2 weeks QA + docs) vs Differentiator (~8–12 weeks with UX & simulated preview). Recommend we commit MVP for this quarter and start spike on Differentiator.

alex: agree. We should also include a kill-switch and per-tenant opt-out.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: create feature-flag `fallback_chain_enabled`, add quota on fallback calls, enable detailed sampling for 2 weeks in prod.

sara: next steps: alex will spec API + open PR for infra changes; julia to draft guardrail checklist; mohit to run prompt eval on quant variants; danny to prepare sales one-pager and legal SLO draft. I'll book a 30m sync Friday to sign off. :calendar: :white_check_mark:

alex: I'll open the PR by EOD and tag everyone.

mohit: starting the eval now, will post results here tomorrow.

julia: will draft runbook + rollback steps.

danny: will draft customer-facing blurb and escalate the two customers who pushed.

sara: thanks all — goal: parity ship for initial deals, then follow up with differentiator UX next quarter. :rocket:
